================================================================================
New Jersey Influenza and Respiratory Illness Surveillance Report
Week ending January 1, 2022 (MMWR Week 52) — Season 2021-22
Source PDF: Flu_Report_Week_2021_52.pdf
================================================================================

HIGHLIGHTS
- Influenza activity level is high statewide
- Emergency Department visits and Outpatient provider visits associated with influenza-like illness are higher than last week and higher than this same week last year
- There have been no influenza-associated confirmed pediatric deaths reported this season
- There have been 8 outbreaks reported from Long-term Care Facilities this season
- Positive results continue to be reported; Influenza A (subtyping not performed) is at 78.43%, followed by A(H3N2) (20.10%), B (1.36%), and A(H1N1)pdm09 (0.11%)

SECTION 1 — Current Influenza Activity Level
Statewide influenza activity remains HIGH for the week ending January 1, 2022, with all six regions (Northwest, Northeast, Central West, Central East, Southwest, Southeast) at HIGH. Cumulative season cases reached 7,213 via PCR and rapid testing, up from 6,079 the prior week. Eight long-term care facility outbreaks have been reported this season and zero confirmed pediatric flu deaths. The activity-level comparison chart shows the 2021-22 season sustaining high activity through weeks 51-52, dramatically earlier and more intense than the suppressed 2020-21 season. The state map shows uniform high geographic spread across all New Jersey regions, consistent with an early, widespread influenza season.

SECTION 2 — Laboratory Testing
PCR results show continued high but slightly moderating current-week positives. This week recorded 598 influenza A subtyping-not-performed, 144 A(H3N2), 6 influenza B, and 0 A(H1N1)pdm09. Past-three-week counts were 2,658, 732, 24, and 4 respectively. Cumulative season totals reached 4,920 (78.43%) A subtyping-not-performed, 1,261 (20.10%) A(H3N2), 85 (1.36%) B, and 7 (0.11%) A(H1N1)pdm09. Rapid influenza testing added 209 positives this week, 643 over three weeks, and 940 cumulatively. Influenza A remains overwhelmingly predominant, with H3N2 the leading subtype where typing was completed; the H3N2 cumulative share edged up to 20.10%.

SECTION 3 — Virologic Surveillance
Virologic charts show positive PCR influenza tests peaking around weeks 50-51 and beginning to decline at week 52, with type AH3 and A-not-typed dominating and minimal type B and 2009 H1N1. The A-subtyping-not-performed weekly chart confirms a sharp peak near 1,100 in mid-to-late December tapering off. Regional bar charts (past-three-weeks and total-to-date) show most regions dominated by A typing-not-performed, with H3N2 prominent in the Northwest, Northeast, and Central West and some 2009 H1N1 in the Southeast. The rapid influenza percent-positive curve for 2021-22 sits above off-season baseline near the three-highest-seasons average, indicating intense but possibly cresting activity statewide.

SECTION 1 — Current Influenza Activity Level
Influenza activity was MODERATE statewide for the week ending January 15, 2022, with all six surveillance regions (Northwest, Northeast, Central West, Central East, Southwest, Southeast) reporting MODERATE activity. The activity-level comparison chart shows the 2021-22 season rising to moderate by early January, well below the high-activity peaks of pre-pandemic seasons but markedly above the suppressed 2020-21 season. Cumulative season totals beginning MMWR week 40 (October 9, 2021) reached 8,142 cases reported (PCR and rapid), 10 outbreaks in long-term care facilities, and 0 confirmed pediatric flu deaths, reflecting a building early-winter influenza wave across New Jersey that has begun to ease slightly from the prior week.

SECTION 2 — Laboratory Testing
PCR laboratory testing for the current week recorded 116 Influenza A (subtyping not performed), 28 Influenza A H3N2, 2 Influenza B, and 0 A(H1N1)pdm09. Past-three-week totals were 1,089 A unsubtyped, 298 H3N2, 13 B, and 0 H1N1pdm09. Cumulative season totals were 5,427 A unsubtyped (77.63%), 1,465 H3N2 (20.95%), 92 B (1.32%), and 7 H1N1pdm09 (0.10%). Rapid influenza testing added 45 current-week positives, 420 over three weeks, and 1,151 cumulatively. The data confirm Influenza A overwhelmingly predominant, with H3N2 the dominant subtype where typing occurred, though current-week counts have declined sharply from the December peak.

SECTION 3 — Virologic Surveillance
The virologic charts show positive typed influenza (PCR) results rising sharply through November-December 2021, peaking around 300-350 positives near the end of December, then declining through early January 2022. Influenza A subtyping-not-performed mirrors this, peaking above 1,000 in late December before falling. Type AH3 dominates with minimal Type B and 2009 H1N1. Regional bar charts show H3/AH3 and untyped A distributed across all regions. The rapid influenza percent-positive line for 2021-22 climbed toward the three-highest-season average through December and is beginning to taper, indicating the early-winter wave may be cresting.
